desc:
The strings s and t are anagrams of each other. In one move you may swap two neighbouring characters of s. Return the minimum number of moves needed to turn s into exactly t.

Example: s = "aabb" and t = "bbaa" need 4 moves (each of the two b letters has to pass both a letters). s = "abc" and t = "cba" need 3 moves.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters
t is a rearrangement of s
hints: A breadth-first search over all reachable strings is hopeless. First decide which letter of s becomes which letter of t.
Equal letters should never be swapped with each other. So the k-th c of s should end at the position of the k-th c of t. This gives you a permutation of positions.
The minimum number of adjacent swaps that sorts a permutation equals its number of inversions. Count them in O(n log n) with a Fenwick tree or merge sort.
editorial: Map every position of s to a target position in t by matching equal letters in order (the k-th occurrence of a letter to the k-th occurrence in t). Matching in order is optimal because swapping two equal letters never helps, and any other matching would cross two equal letters which only adds inversions.

After the mapping, perm[i] is the final position of the letter now at i. Each adjacent swap changes the number of inversions of perm by exactly one, and the target (identity permutation) has none, so the answer is the number of inversions of perm: pairs i < j with perm[i] > perm[j].

Count inversions with a Fenwick tree: scan left to right, add the number of earlier elements larger than the current one, then insert the current one. That gives O(n log n) time and O(n) space. The result may be about n²/4, i.e. up to 16 million here.
solution:
def minAdjacentSwaps(s, t):
    n = len(s)
    pos = {}
    for j in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        pos.setdefault(t[j], []).append(j)
    perm = [pos[c].pop() for c in s]
    tree = [0] * (n + 2)
    inv = 0
    for idx, v in enumerate(perm):
        # count earlier elements with value <= v
        x = v + 1
        le = 0
        while x > 0:
            le += tree[x]
            x -= x & -x
        inv += idx - le
        x = v + 1
        while x <= n:
            tree[x] += 1
            x += x & -x
    return inv
